align.prompt: LLM ablation baseline: maximise horizontal/vertical segments for as-twn-kaohsiung-shape-rect (orig).

transcript.note: Round 1. The 10 already-H/V segments are the prescribed square ring (c=1..13 x r=1..13, verts 4,11,6,7,14,16,0,3,15,13) — locked, nothing touches them. Only the 7 non-ring points can move. (1) Hub 8(6,9) has all four of its edges landing on frozen ring vertices 4(1,5)/16(13,8)/3(8,13)/7(9,1), so a single cell decides everything: r=8 closes 8-16 into H and c=8 closes 8-3 into V, so 8 -> (8,8) takes two at once (criterion 1, and 3 in that it puts 8-3-5 on one column). The rival cell (9,8) also scores two (8-7 V + 8-16 H) but leaves nothing collinear; c=8 and c=9 are mutually exclusive so two is the ceiling here within +-3. (2) 10(14,7): the obvious V with 16 would be c=13, but that column IS the ring's right edge 16-14, so 10 would be swallowed onto a line and 16-10 would overlap it — took the other intersection instead, r=8 (H with 16) meets c=16 (V with 12) at (16,8), both segments aligned, nothing overlapping. (3) North dangling chain 3-5-9-1: 5 cannot take r=13 (that row is the ring's top edge 15-3 / 0-3, again a swallow), so 5 -> (8,14) makes 5-3 vertical, 9 -> (8,15) continues the same column (9-5 V, straight through 5), and 1 -> (4,15) closes 1-9 into H. All moves are 1-2 cells, all land on empty cells, and every relative order only degrades to a tie (never reverses), which is what H/V alignment requires. Left alone deliberately: 7-2, because 2 -> r=1 would run along the ring's bottom edge and swallow vertex 14(13,1), and the vertical alternative is 6 cells west, over the +-3 limit; 4-8 and 8-7 are the two edges hub 8 had to give up.
